migration.notes: 51 of 51 coverage entries replayed clean (references, labels, move-result, branch offsets, register moves, register flow, return types); the battery toggle row is withheld, see migration/coverage-exclusions.json. The custom hunks are gated by migration/hunk-contracts.json plus scripts/verify_214_custom_hunks.py, which re-derives every entry from the 194 delta (instruction shape and frame growth, payload literals, the reviewed splice recomputed from the 214 upstream, the register/encoding law, the contracts, the custom-only surfaces, and the type each register provably holds where a hunk reads it) and is enforced by scripts/migrate_214.py; scripts/selftest_214_hunk_gate.py corrupts one reviewed property at a time to prove the gate goes red. The type walk is also run over the pristine 214 tree (--type-flow-control), which reports nothing; it is what the first 214 build failed on (VerifyError in hi1.d), and scripts/port_214_candidate.py now mirrors a customization's register rename onto the line the port keeps, recorded per line in migration/port-report.json. A second device crash came from the other direction: a `replace` hunk carried the register numbering of the frame it was written in (`Ljk5;->c` handed the `Ljava/lang/String;` slot v14 to `Lcom/box/app/vpn/VpnBridge;->key(Lbr5;)I` because 194 kept that enum in v14 and 214 moved it to v15), so scripts/port_214_candidate.py now also re-spells a replaced line's operands from the two versions of the line it replaces (1 line, recorded in migration/port-report.json under registerRealignments), and the type-flow gate was widened from "uncast Object in a narrowed slot" to any mismatch it can prove from this tree's class hierarchy - with the pristine 214 tree still reporting nothing. A third device crash was not a verifier rejection at all: `Resources$NotFoundException: String resource ID #0x0` from the core-detail row, because the reviewed placement for `Lpa1;->a(` kept 194's `const/4 v15, 0x0` flag clear while 214 reads the string resource id in v15 and the flag in v4 - the arm zeroed the id it had just computed. The pin lost that line (its `evidence` now names all three register roles) and scripts/verify_214_custom_hunks.py gained an eighth gate, check_grafted_arm_roles, which re-derives every anchor+insert placement and reports a value the arm takes from an invoke being re-written before the jump onto a merge that still reads it; scripts/selftest_214_hunk_gate.py corrupts that line back in to prove it (13 rows). Integers, so no type walk and no name-based check can see it - which is why the gate now also checks the reviewed placements against themselves. A fourth device crash came from the same arm one step further: `NullPointerException ... Object.getClass() on a null object reference` at `v74.d` called from `ba1.c:573`, because 214 reuses the flag register for something live - every stock arm that reaches `:goto_6` does `move-object/from16 v22, v4` before `const/4 v4, 0x0`, since the merge hands `v22` to `Lv74;->d(...)` as its `Lyw1;` argument - while 194 zeroed an idle register and carried no spill, so the reviewed placement had to gain that move (7 lines to 8) and the ported method is again byte-identical to the 214 upstream except for those 8 lines. scripts/verify_214_custom_hunks.py gained a ninth gate, check_grafted_arm_spills, the mirror of the eighth: it reads the reviewed `insert` (located by its `anchor`) rather than the tree, collects every arm of the ported file that jumps to the same label, and only when saving-before-reusing is that release's habit for all of them does it require the grafted arm to do the same - so a pin that omits a line cannot silence the check by omitting it from the tree too. The same pass removed the placement's now-inert `tolerates` entry: an exemption that covers no difference keeps silencing that literal class for the plan, so the gate now reports a reviewed tolerance nothing needs. scripts/selftest_214_hunk_gate.py grows to 15 rows and learns `@pins`, a mutation of a copy of migration/manual-pins.json, for the two gates that read the reviewed placement: the spill taken back out, and a tolerance invented for nothing. A fifth device crash was the verifier again, on a class no hand placement had ever touched: `VerifyError ... register v31 has type Reference: android.content.Context but expected Reference: qe2` in `Lv86;->e(Ljava/lang/Object;Ljava/lang/Object;)Ljava/lang/Object;` - `v86` being 194's `sv5`, whose body came over through whole-method alignment. That alignment grafted two identical 5-line runs that call `Lcom/box/app/cfg/CfgNav;->wrap`; a `/range` call needs a contiguous span, so each run copies its arguments into v14/v15/v16 and the copy clobbers all three, not just the result slot. 194 could reuse v16 there because in that frame it is not read again before it is rewritten; 214 reads it again 29 instructions later (`move-object/from16 v31, v16`) to fill the `Lqe2;` slot of `Lb96;-><init>`, and ART rejected the class - `apktool b` was silent, since v16 is a legal register and `.locals 52` still covers it. Which numbers a grafted block may clobber is a fact about the frame it was written in rather than about the call, and this block has no merge point to consult, so gates 8 and 9 could not see it. scripts/port_214_candidate.py now re-anchors a colliding staging span to the highest contiguous span of registers the method never reads again (v49/v50/v51 in `v86`) and refuses to guess when the frame has nothing dead left, reporting `no dead span` for a human placement instead; the block keeps its shape, so the only file that differs from the previous candidate is smali/v86.smali, 4 lines, same length, and migration/port-report.json records the decision under graftScratch. Liveness for both sides of it - the porter picking registers, the gate judging them - lives in one reviewed module, scripts/smali_liveness.py, which follows the method's own successors and catch entries rather than the text below, because a branch can step over a read and a write on every path that reaches it frees the register. The gate gained a tenth check, check_grafted_staging, that diffs every grafted run (reviewed placements and alignment additions alike) against the 214 upstream and reports a staged register the release still needs; it is the same rule on both sides of the hop: 0 findings on the 194 custom tree, which ships with that identical block, 1 on the broken candidate, 0 on the fixed one. scripts/selftest_214_hunk_gate.py grows to 16 rows, the new one putting v86's staging span back on v14/v15/v16.
